decisive_items: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified (hematoxylin-eosin staining, original magnification ×40)
Patient had history of kidney transplant in 2004 causing immunocompromised status.
Two distinct, well-defined, umbilicated skin-colored lesions measuring 2 × 2 cm each located over the glabella and right cheek with central ulceration and hemorrhagic crusting
response.rationale: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos in an immunocompromised patient with umbilicated cutaneous nodules strongly indicate Cryptococcosis; the halo corresponds to the cryptococcal capsule. Histoplasmosis also shows intracellular yeasts but lacks the characteristic surrounding halo, and BCC would not show yeast organisms on histopathology.

rejected.why: The dermal infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages is nonspecific and does not outweigh the specific finding of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos, which is characteristic of Cryptococcus rather than Histoplasma.

Arborizing telangiectasias and ulceration are dermoscopic features of BCC, but the histopathological identification of intracellular yeasts with halos is definitive and excludes a purely epithelial tumor.
